The app runs on the user's own keys. Left: one row per source with key status, budget today, last success, last error, Enabled, Save; then catalogues and freshness. Right: key entry per source (BrickLink takes four values), picture priority. Rows: configured at four widths; the six key entry states; no keys with catalogue not loaded; budget used up; key rejected with catalogue loading.

12nCollection sync
Bring an existing collection in from Rebrickable, Brickset or BrickLink using the configured keys (12l), work on it here, then send the changes back. Pull shows every difference first and never deletes here; Send shows the changes first and asks before removing anything there. A source card shows the link, scopes, last pull and send, and what is waiting. Rows: sources at four widths; link a collection; pull preview; send review; changed in both places; sending, sent, paused, key rejected; no keys.

How sync works
Pull never deletes anything here. Items that are only here are listed for you to decide.
Send always shows the changes first and asks before it removes anything there.
The collection here is the one you work on. Each source keeps its own link.
Each run uses the source's daily budget (Catalogues & keys).

How sync works
Pull never deletes anything here. Items that are only here are listed for you to decide.
Send always shows the changes first and asks before it removes anything there.
The collection here is the one you work on. Each source keeps its own link.

12oScan a set barcode
Add (4d) gets a barcode scanner. Phone: the camera reads the EAN on the box, a sheet shows the matching set with a condition selector (Sealed, New, Used), copies, storage and price paid, then adds it; Keep scanning returns to the camera with an Undo toast. Desktop and iPad: camera or USB scanner into one field, a session list with condition per set, and one add for all. Barcodes are looked up on Brickset with the configured key.
